question: In a ΔMNR, the sides MN and MR are extended to P and Q, respectively. The bisectors of ∠ PNR and ∠ QRN intersect at a point X. If angle X = 75°, then the value of 2 ∠M is:
solution:
Angle formed by external bisectors intersection: ∠X = 90° − ∠M / 2

⇒ 75° = 90° − ∠M / 2

⇒ ∠M / 2 = 90° − 75° = 15°

⇒ ∠M = 30° ⇒ 2 × ∠M = 60°

**∴ Answer = 60°**

**Given:**

In triangle MNR, sides MN and MR are extended to P and Q. Bisectors of exterior angles ∠PNR and ∠QRN meet at X. Angle ∠X = 75°.

**Formula used:**

Angle at intersection of external bisectors = 90° − (Internal opposite angle / 2)

 
 
• 
• 
• 
• M N R P Q X = 75° ∠X = 90° − ∠M/2 

**Calculations:**

∠X = 90° − ∠M/2

⇒ 75° = 90° − ∠M/2

⇒ ∠M/2 = 90° − 75°

⇒ ∠M/2 = 15°

⇒ ∠M = 15° × 2 = 30°

⇒ 2∠M = 2 × 30° = 60°

**∴ The correct answer is 60°. (Option 4)**
